rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is phrased as a report but functions as a command, like the instruction that mothers nurse their children.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن لفظها خبر ومعناها أمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A menstruating divorcee waits three qurūʾ; a pregnant divorcee until delivery; a premenarchal or postmenopausal divorcee three months; pregnant widows until delivery, and other widows four months and ten days.
rows.anchor: والعدة على ضربين: عدة المطلقة وعدة المتوفى عنها زوجها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enslaved women's applicable waiting periods are half of a free woman's, so their menstrual waiting period is two qurūʾ; an unconsummated divorce entails no waiting period.
rows.anchor: وعدة الإماء فيما له نصف ومن الأقراء قرآن

rows.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم
rows.claim: Ikrima and Ibrahim take what God created in the wombs to mean menstrual blood.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة وإبراهيم: يعني الحيض،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Muqatil take the phrase to mean a child, that is, pregnancy.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل: يعني الحمل في الولد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women must not hide menstruation or pregnancy to defeat a husband's right of return or a child's claim; a woman is trusted about her sexual parts.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآية لا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن من الحيض والحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿūla means husbands, plural of baʿl; baʿl originally means master or owner, and the husband is so called for managing his wife's affairs. The verse about worshipping Baal is cited.
rows.anchor: وبعولتهن أزواجهن، وهو جمع بعل،

rows.speaker: مسلم بن محارب
rows.claim: Muslim ibn Muharib reads the tāʾ in buʿūlatuhunna with sukūn because of the succession of vowelled sounds.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن محارب وبعولتهن بإسكان التاء لكثرة الحركات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī prefers the usual vocalized form as more eloquent, fitting, and sound.
rows.anchor: والاتباع أفصح وأحسن وأوفق وأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband may return his wife during her waiting period if he seeks reconciliation; he must not use repeated return near the end of the period to harm her.
rows.anchor: أحق أولى بردهن أي برجعتهن في ذلك أي في حال العدة إن أرادوا إصلاحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women have rights over their husbands corresponding to the rights husbands have over them, according to proper custom.
rows.anchor: ولهن أي وللنساء على أزواجهن مثل الذي عليهن من الحق

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about a wife's rights, the Prophet says her husband must not strike her face or insult her, must feed and clothe her as he does himself, and must not abandon her.
rows.anchor: يروى أن امرأة معاذ قالت: يا رسول الله ما حق الزوجة على زوجها؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urges kind treatment of women, describing them as dependent wards entrusted to husbands by God's trust and made lawful through God's word.
rows.anchor: المبارك بن فضالة عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «استوصوا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Maimuna, the Prophet praises spouses who serve one another: wives who comply except in sin receive the stated reward of a thousand martyrs, and gentle husbands the reward of a hundred.
rows.anchor: وعن ميمونة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Answering Umar, the Prophet says women may surpass men in reward, a wife's contentment and prayer elevate her husband, and betraying him is grave after shirk; he warns about orphans and women and equates wives' rights with his own.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه) : يا رسول الله فكيف يكون للمرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī glosses the men's degree over women as superiority in merit.
rows.anchor: بالمعروف وللرجال عليهن درجة في الفضل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the degree by the dowry and financial support a man provides his wife.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view explains the degree as a difference in intellect.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال، وقيل: بالعقل،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view explains the degree by inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالعقل، وقيل: بالميراث، وقيل: بالدرجة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported view says the degree itself is the explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالميراث، وقيل: بالدرجة، قال قتادة: بالجهاد.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the men's degree with jihad.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: بالجهاد. عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A woman representing women asks about their reward when men fight and die; the Prophet replies that obedience to husbands and recognition of their rights equal that service, though few women do so.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: بينما نحن عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that women came to the Prophet saying men had gained virtue through jihad and asking what deed remained for women in God's path.
rows.anchor: ثابت عن أنس، قال: جئن إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلن:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked whether women have jihad, the Prophet calls their jihad guarding their zeal and struggling against themselves; patient women are fighters and garrisoned, with two rewards.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن الحصين قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل على النساء جهاد؟

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view explains the men's degree as divorce and return.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالطلاق والرجعة، وقيل: بالشهادة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view explains the degree as testimony.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالشهادة، وقيل: بقوة العبادة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view explains the degree as strength in worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالشهادة، وقيل: بقوة العبادة،

rows.speaker: سفيان وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam explain the degree as authority or governance.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان وزيد بن أسلم: بالإمارة.

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the degree means a virtue or advantage concerning rights.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي: معناه: وللرجال عليهن درجة أي فضيلة للحق.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A woman complained to Aisha that her husband repeatedly divorced and returned her to cause harm; in the pre-Islamic period he could return before the waiting period ended without a limit on divorces, so the verse capped divorce at three.
rows.anchor: روى هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أن امرأة أتتها فشكت أن زوجها

words: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two divorces are those permitting return: retain her properly or release her graciously; after one or two, return is possible during the waiting period, after it she controls remarriage, and a third divorce bars return until another marriage.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: معنى الآية الطلاق الذي يملك فيه الرجعة مرتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband may not take back any of what he gave his wife in dowry or other property at separation, except when both fear they cannot uphold God's limits, allowing khulʿ.
rows.anchor: ولا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا في حال الاستبدال والطلاق مما آتيتموهن شيئا

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The account of Jamilah, daughter of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Awfa, and Thabit ibn Qays says she hated him despite his love, sought separation, and agreed to return his garden; the Prophet told him to take only the garden and release her.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في جميلة بنت عبد الله بن أبي أوفى تزوجها ثابت بن قيس بن شماس

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the continuation of Jamilah and Thabit's case, she says she is not accusing him of being a bad man but hates him; he takes back the garden, releases her, and this is called Islam's first khulʿ and the occasion for the verse.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا ثابت خذ منها ما أعطيتها وخل سبيلها» ففعل،

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Abu reads the phrase as yathunnā, using zann in the sense of knowing.
rows.anchor: تصديقه قراءة أبي: إلا أن يظنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī takes the poetic use of akhāf in Mihjan's line to mean I know, supporting the gloss of the reading yathunnā.
rows.anchor: فلا تدفنني بالفلاة فإنني … أخاف إذا ما مت أن لا أذوقها

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وحمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Hamza, and Yaʿqub read the verb passively; Abu Ubayd prefers this on the basis of Ibn Masud's reading and the following wording, which assigns the fear to others.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة ويعقوب: (يخافا) بضم الياء

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fear is that a wife will fall into sin through disobedience to her husband, or that the husband will overstep if she does not obey him.
rows.anchor: وهو أن تخاف المرأة الفتنة على نفسها فتعصي الله في أمر زوجها،

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids taking a wife's property without her consent unless nushuz or bad conduct comes from her, such as refusing her husband's oath, command, or bed; her voluntary ransom is permitted.
rows.anchor: فنهى الله تعالى الرجل أن يأخذ من امرأة شيئا بغير رضاها إلا أن يكون النشوز وسوء الخلق من قبلها

words: إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking more than the dowry given is disliked, though legally valid.
rows.anchor: ويكره أن يأخذ منها أكثر مما أعطاها، ولكنه في الحكم جائز.

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ
rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar imprisons a woman who refuses her husband and threatens self-harm; after three nights she says she found rest away from him, so he calls this nushuz and tells the husband to divorce her for whatever she offers, even her earrings.
rows.anchor: يبين ذلك ما روى الحكم بن عيينة أن امرأة نشزت على زوجها في إمارة عمر بن الخطاب

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ
rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the dual pronoun refers to the husband alone, though both spouses are named because they form a pair; he compares the verse's dual wording with cases where only one member acts and cites a poem as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أراد به الزوج دون المرأة فذكرهما جميعا لأقرانهما

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ
rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others take no blame to apply to both: a woman may seek ransom if she fears harm or sin, and a husband may accept what she freely gives, though she may not otherwise waste property without right.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم معناه: فلا جناح عليهما جميعا، لا جناح على المرأة

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One juristic view, held by Ibn Abbas and the early Iraqi position of al-Shafiʿi, treats khulʿ as annulment rather than divorce; al-Shafiʿi later retracted it in Egypt.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: إنه فسخ بلا طلاق، وهو قول ابن عباس،

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِ
rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان والشافعي
rows.claim: The other juristic view, attributed to Uthman and al-Shafiʿi's later position, counts khulʿ as one irrevocable divorce unless the husband intends more.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني: إن الخلع تطليقة بائنة إلا أن ينوي أكثر منها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's bounds are His commands and prohibitions; whoever exceeds them is among the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: تلك حدود الله هذه أوامر الله ونواهيه فلا تعتدوها فلا تجاوزوها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the middle prayer as dawn: it lies between night and day, is especially liable to be missed, cannot be shortened or combined, and lies between prayers that can be combined.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: هي صلاة الصبح،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn interpretation is supported by the verse saying the dawn recitation is witnessed by angels of both night and day and entered in both registers.
rows.anchor: وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا يعني تشهده ملائكة الليل

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They infer dawn from the following command to stand devoutly, saying dawn is the only prescribed prayer with qunut.
rows.anchor: قالوا: ولا صلاة مكتوبة فيها قنوت سوى صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Raja says Ibn Abbas led dawn at Basra, performed qunut before bowing with raised hands, and identified it as the middle prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء العطاردي: صلى بنا ابن عباس في مسجد البصرة صلاة الغداة،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Hanzala reports from Anas that the Prophet performed qunut for a month and continued qunut in the dawn prayer until his death.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه ما روى حنظلة عن أنس قال: قنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شهرا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet and each of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali continued qunut until death.
rows.anchor: ابن أبي ليلى عن عطاء بن أبي رباح عن ابن عباس قال: قنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى مات،

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وأبو سعيد الخدري وأسامة بن زيد وعائشة
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Usama ibn Zayd, and Aisha identify the middle prayer as Dhuhr.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي صلاة الظهر وهو قول زيد بن ثابت وأبي سعيد الخدري وأسامة بن زيد وعائشة.

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd reports that Dhuhr at midday was hardest for the Companions to attend, so the Prophet considered burning the houses of absentees; the verse then descended.
rows.anchor: روى عروة عن زيد بن ثابت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي بالهاجرة وكانت أثقل الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Dhuhr view calls it the middle of daytime prayers; it was the first prayer obligated, the first prayed facing the Kaaba, and the prayer for which Friday congregations are raised.
rows.anchor: ولأنها أوسط صلوات النهار، ومن خصائصها أنها أول صلاة فرضت،

rows.speaker: علي وعبد الله وأبو هريرة والنخعي وزر بن حبيش وقتادة وأبو أيوب والضحاك والكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ali, Abd Allah, Abu Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿi, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Qatada, Abu Ayyub, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil identify it as Asr; Abu Hanifa chooses this view.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هي صلاة العصر، وهو قول علي وعبد الله وأبي هريرة والنخعي وزر بن حبيش وقتادة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Samura quotes the Prophet explicitly identifying the middle prayer as Asr.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى الحسن عن سمرة بن جندب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «صلاة

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Some reports say the prayer Solomon neglected was the middle prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار هي التي فرط فيها سليمان عليه السلام

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara says the first revealed wording named Asr, then was replaced by the middle prayer; when told this meant Asr, he replied that he had related its revelation and abrogation, and God knows best.
rows.anchor: سفيان بن عيينة عن البراء بن عازب قال: نزلت حافظوا على الصلوات وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: حفصة
rows.claim: Hafsa told her codex scribe to write that she heard the Prophet call the middle prayer Asr.
rows.anchor: نافع عن حفصة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها قالت لكاتب مصحفها: إذا بلغت مواقيت الصلاة

rows.speaker: عائشة وأبي بن كعب وعبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Aisha's codex read the middle prayer as Asr, as did Ubay ibn Kaʿb and Ubayd ibn Umayr.
rows.anchor: هشام عن عروة عن أبيه قال كان في مصحف عائشة حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the Battle of the Trench, the Prophet said the enemy had kept them from the middle prayer, Asr, and prayed it between Maghrib and Isha.
rows.anchor: الأعمش عن مسلم عن شتير بن شكل عن علي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الأحزاب: «شغلونا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man recounts that, when asked to identify the middle prayer, the Prophet mapped the fingers to dawn, Dhuhr, Maghrib, and Isha, then identified the remaining middle one as Asr.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن رجلا قال في مجلس عبد العزيز بن مروان: أرسلني أبو بكر وعمر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Supporters of Asr say it falls between two daytime and two nighttime prayers, and that the Prophet then gave it special attention.
rows.anchor: قالوا: ولأنها بين صلاتي نهار وصلاتي ليل،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Basra reports the Prophet saying earlier communities neglected Asr; whoever observes it receives twice the reward, and there is no prayer after it until the evening star appears.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو تميم الحبشاني عن أبي بصرة الغفاري قال: صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة العصر،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet commands people to pray early on cloudy days, warning that missing Asr nullifies one's deeds.
rows.anchor: أبو قلابة عن أبي المهاجر عن بريدة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «بكروا بالصلاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports a saying of the Prophet about the one who prays Asr being safeguarded in family and property.
rows.anchor: نافع عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الذي يصلي العصر

rows.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
rows.claim: Qubaysa ibn Dhuʾayb identifies the middle prayer as Maghrib: it is intermediate in length, is not shortened in travel, and is the daytime prayer with an odd number of units.
rows.anchor: وقال قبيصة بن ذؤيب: هي صلاة المغرب، ألا ترى أنها واسطة ليست بأقلها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet calling Maghrib the best prayer, neither waived for travelers nor residents; it opens the night prayer and closes the day, and post-prayer units bring the stated heavenly reward and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن أفضل الصلوات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A view relayed by Abu Maytham Sahl ibn Muhammad identifies the middle prayer as the later Isha, since it lies between two prayers that are not shortened.
rows.anchor: وحكى الشيخ أبو ميثم سهل بن محمد عن بعضهم أنها صلاة العشاء الأخيرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uthman reports the Prophet saying that praying Isha in congregation equals half a night's worship and praying dawn in congregation equals a whole night.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمر عن عثمان بن عفان (رضي الله عنه) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من صلى العشاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the middle prayer is one of the five but leave it unidentified; al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym asks whether knowing it would make someone preserve it while neglecting the rest, and concludes that observing all five preserves it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هي إحدى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says God left the middle prayer unidentified to prompt people to observe all prayers.
rows.anchor: وبه قال أبو بكر الوراق، قال: لو شاء الله عز وجل لبينها، ولكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī endorses leaving the middle prayer unnamed so people preserve all prayers hoping to catch it, as God likewise hid Laylat al-Qadr, the Greatest Name, and Friday's answering hour as wisdom and mercy.
rows.anchor: قال الثعلبي [ولقد أحسنا] في قوليهما فإن الله تعالى أخفى الصلاة الوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle-prayer wording shows witr is not obligatory: obligatory prayers are more than three and fewer than seven, and only five can be an odd number with a middle position.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله عز وجل والصلاة الوسطى دليل على أن الوتر ليس بواجب وذلك أن المسلمين اتفقوا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asks how many prayers are obligatory; the Prophet answers five, and says the man enters Paradise if truthful in neither adding nor subtracting.
rows.anchor: قتادة عن أنس قال: قال رجل: يا رسول الله، كم افترض الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Bedouin asks about Islam; the Prophet names five daily prayers, Ramadan fasting, and zakat, with only voluntary acts beyond them, and says the man succeeds if truthful in doing no more or less.
rows.anchor: وعن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال: جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل نجد

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: When told that Abu Muhammad called witr obligatory, Ubada calls him a liar and cites the Prophet: five prayers are prescribed, and one who fulfills them has God's pledge of Paradise, while one who neglects them may be punished or forgiven.
rows.anchor: فقال عبادة: كذب أبو محمد، سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «خمس صلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line about Banu Ghudana witnesses the use of rijālan for people walking on foot, contrasted with riding mounts.
rows.anchor: وبنو غدانة شاخص أبصارهم … يمشون تحت بطونهن رجالا

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Rukbānan is the plural of rider; al-Mufaddal says rākib is used only for a camel rider, while a horse, donkey, or mule rider is named for that animal.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع راكب، قال المفضل: لا يقال راكب إلا لصاحب الجمل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijālan and rukbānan are accusative circumstantial expressions: pray walking or riding.
rows.anchor: ونصبت على الحال، أي فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When fear prevents a person from praying with full devotional posture and due observance, prayer while walking or riding suffices.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: فإن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين الصلاة حقها لخوف

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators describe prayer amid battle or pursuit facing any direction, mounted or walking, with prostration lower than bowing and gestures; this is severe-fear prayer, discussed again in Surat al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: هذا في المسابقة والمطاردة، يصلي حيث يولي وجهه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permitted causes of such fear include combat or pursuit, a raging beast, an attacking camel, a rushing flood, or any situation in which death is the prevailing expectation.
rows.anchor: والخوف الذي يجوز للمصلي أن يصلي من أجله راكبا أو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Severe-fear prayer is two rakʿahs, though one rakʿah is also valid.
rows.anchor: وإن صلى صلاة الأمن فله أن يصلي صلاة شدة الخوف وهي ركعتان، فإن صلاها ركعة واحدة جاز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying prayer was prescribed as four rakʿahs at home, two while traveling, and one in fear.
rows.anchor: لما روى مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: فرض الله عز وجل الصلاة على لسان نبيكم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when armies clash and people exchange blows, one should say tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, and takbir and remember God; that is the prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إذا كنت في القتال، والتقى الزحفان،

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says that if a person cannot even do that, they should still remember God inwardly.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري: فإن لم يستطع فلا يدع ذكرها في نفسه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe, worshippers should perform the five prayers fully and fulfill their due observances, as God taught them what they did not know.
rows.anchor: فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله أي فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة لحقوقها كما علمكم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says Arabs most often call a woman zawja, while the Quran uses zawj in the bequest to wives.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: أكثر ما تقول العرب للمرأة زوجة، ولكن في القرآن زوج

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو وأبو عامر والأعمش وحمزة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Amr, Abu Amir, al-Aʿmash, and Hamza read waṣiyyatan in the accusative, as an instruction to make a bequest; the rest read it nominatively as a prescribed bequest. Other glosses are proposed, and Ibn Masud's reading supports the latter sense.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو وأبو عامر والأعمش وحمزة (وصية) بالنصب على معنى فليوصوا وصية،
